title: Set a printer paper tray's guides snug to a fresh A4 stack
instruction: Set this tray's paper guides for the A4 paper so it feeds straight: the stack square against the feed edge and lying flat, every guide against it but not squeezing it. Then let go.
context: Refilling a household or office printer is familiar. Paper dropped in crooked or guides left at another size can feed poorly. This custom cassette preserves squaring loose A4 paper, squeezing guide latches, adjusting linked width guides and a rear guide, then easing pressure and letting go. Sprung faces make excessive squeeze observable as displacement.
setup: Custom fabrication cassette: fabrication/README.md supplies drawings, editable manufacturing profiles, BOM, spring specifications, sources and assembly/calibration. Coordinates in mm above the station table: paper centre x=270; feed face y=-160; floor 304 x 417, opening 292 x 396; enclosed 35 mm plinth and 3 mm floor, paper surface z=38; front panel top z=100. Width faces start at x=161/379, span y=-70..30, linked 1:1 with 70 mm inward travel each. Rear face starts y=196, spans x=200..340 and travels 150 mm. Three 3 mm pads have 5 mm travel, combined spring-rate target 1.500 N/mm, 30 mm cartridges and direct calibrated 0..5 mm scales. Blue near-width and rear latches are 30 mm wide, top z=97, hinge z=71. Squeeze near 0.10 rad releases 0.5 mm pitch square pawls; stop at 0.17 rad. A released pawl must reach an aligned tooth, with a small settling slide if needed. Four loose 25-sheet A4 groups, each 210 x 297 x 2.5 mm, 125 g; no handles or binding. Lot A bottom-to-top leading-midpoint offsets before yaw: 3/20/37/54 mm behind feed face; x offsets +0.8/-0.6/+0.5/-0.8 mm; yaw +0.4/-0.5/+0.7/-0.3 deg. Lot B reverses feed offsets and x/yaw signs. Model initial 0.2 mm layer gaps settle. Clamp the cassette to the table. Design unbuilt and calibration records blank; numerical mechanisms and material estimates are described in README.
scoring: End score, averaged over lots A and B. All tiers require finite readable states, released levers and engaged pawls, and every gripper/fingertip face more than 5 mm from paper and moving guide hardware for 1 s. During that second paper/guide motion must be below 5 mm/s and paper angular speed below 0.1 rad/s. All four groups must be inside the cassette and supported on the floor or adjacent layer, with actual surface separation -0.25..+1 mm and centre over support; identity order is unrestricted. Tilt <=2 deg, highest corner <=11.5 mm above floor, pad compression <=2 mm; no guide/feed/wall penetration beyond the 0.25 mm numerical contact allowance. Then award 0.5 for rear-guide gap <=1 mm plus every group yaw <=1 deg and leading edge <=1 mm from feed; independently award 0.5 only when every group has a gap <=1 mm to each width guide. Opposite fanned groups touching opposite guides do not qualify. Contact uses the actual finite 100/140 mm guide spans, not remote corners. On hardware use visible inspection, calibrated scales/indicators and feelers; require reading plus uncertainty within upper limits. Missing or ambiguous measurements cannot certify a tier. Compression is a squeeze proxy, not measured paper bowing; see README and fabrication/CALIBRATION.md.
reset_notes: 1. Inspect and clamp the cassette, complete fabrication calibration, remove damaged paper and keep the mechanism fixed across lots. 2. Squeeze latches, set unloaded width faces 218 mm apart and rear face 356 mm from feed; release, verify pawl engagement and zero all pad pointers. 3. Count four loose 25-sheet groups; place lot A or B using the exact signed midpoint/yaw table in README, then remove all rulers/templates. 4. After the trial remove paper, inspect damage and return guides/pointers to the same datums; do not change springs, tooth phase or drag between lots.
fidelity: Unbuilt custom cassette; dimensions/load targets, no hardware data. Four rigid paper groups omit buckling; >2 mm pad travel is a squeeze proxy. Drive locks approximate square pawls. Active far-guide tracking omits reciprocal loads and gear backlash. Viscous 30 Ns/m differs from dry drag and breakaway. Mass/friction/damping are estimates. Small hardware uses conservative envelopes and joint laws; gauges need calibration. Two initial fans share target settings, allowing replay.
scores: Native scripted demo, this exact source, 600 steps: 1.0 in lot A and 1.0 in lot B. Dream-1, same source and settings: 0 in both lots; it did not reach the cassette in 30 s. Earlier media and scores do not apply to this revision.
